forces.title: Refined product shortages and soaring prices in Europe
forces.description: Disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and damage to Gulf refineries, coupled with offline Russian refining capacity, are straining the global refining system. European refineries operate at near full capacity but face efficiency losses due to crude grade mismatches, leading to lower yields of critical transport fuels like jet fuel and diesel. Consequently, European inventories of jet fuel and gasoline are at five-year minimums, exposing the region to potential shortages and sustained higher prices for auto fuels and ATF.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Risk of LPG rationing due to global energy supply disruptions
forces.description: The global energy system is grappling with significant supply disruptions, exemplified by the Strait of Hormuz crisis. While inventories and bypass pipelines have provided some resilience, vulnerable societies could face genuine shortages and rationing, particularly for fuels like LPG. An example in India showed LPG for commercial use being rationed to protect households. This highlights an ongoing risk for LPG cylinder distribution to households in Europe, where energy security concerns could lead to similar protective measures impacting commercial supplies.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Increased global oil trade rewiring away from Middle East
forces.description: The Strait of Hormuz disruption has triggered a significant rewiring of global oil trade flows, with more than one out of five barrels of seaborne oil rerouted in Q2 2026. This shift aims to reduce exposure to geographic chokepoints and diversify supply, driven by regions like the US increasing exports and new pipelines bypassing the Strait. This ongoing structural change will likely lead to more diversified sourcing for European refiners and marketers, potentially altering traditional supply chains for auto fuels and ATF.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Elevated global inflation driven by refined fuel price increases
forces.description: Supply disruptions, particularly affecting refined fuels, have translated into higher global prices. The IMF raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 4.7% from 3.8% pre-conflict, largely due to these energy price increases. For Oil & Gas Downstream — Marketing & Retail, this cyclical pressure translates to higher input costs for fuel acquisition and potentially constrained consumer spending on auto fuels, although the impact on European oil consumption has so far been limited.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Growing long-term energy security concerns reshaping resilience investments
forces.description: The current energy disruptions, especially the Strait of Hormuz crisis, have moved energy security to the forefront of strategic decision-making. Despite existing shock absorbers like strategic petroleum reserves, their limits are becoming apparent. This concern is leading to increased investment in structural energy security levers, including electrification, clean energy, and alternative oil/gas supply. While essential for overall energy stability, these long-term shifts could divert investment from or alter the demand landscape for traditional fossil fuel marketing and retail infrastructure.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Accelerating EV adoption in the EU threatens auto fuel demand
forces.description: Electrification is being pursued as a key structural lever to enhance energy security by replacing oil and gas in end uses. While global EV sales flatlined in H1 2026, the European Union saw robust growth exceeding 30% in Q2 2026, supported by policies like AccelerateEU. This accelerating adoption of electric vehicles directly reduces demand for traditional auto fuels (gasoline, diesel), posing a significant long-term structural headwind for fuel retail networks and auto fuels marketing in the region.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

forces.title: Plans for new strategic refined product reserves in advanced economies
forces.description: In response to energy security concerns and thinning refined product inventories, advanced economies are planning to expand their strategic product reserves. While specific plans for European countries are not detailed, Australia's announcement of a new 1 billion liter diesel and jet fuel reserve indicates a global trend. If European nations adopt similar strategies, this would create additional demand for refined products and provide a crucial buffer against future supply shocks, benefiting downstream marketing and retail.
forces.source_title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis

viewpoints.title: Global energy system shows resilience but refined fuel security remains vulnerable
viewpoints.description: McKinsey's 'Aftershocks' report highlights that while the energy system has absorbed much of the Strait of Hormuz shock through bypass pipelines and inventory releases, refined product markets face rising stress. Refineries are running at full capacity but struggling with efficiency losses from suboptimal crude grades, leading to lower yields of essential transport fuels like jet fuel and diesel. Inventories of refined products in Europe are hitting five-year lows, raising concerns about potential shortages and sustained higher prices, particularly if the crisis prolongs. This outlook signals continued volatility and vulnerability for downstream marketing and retail.
